What the council says about Mansfield roofs

The district has eleven conservation areas, among them The Park, Market Place, Bridge Street, West Gate, Mansfield Woodhouse and Crow Hill Drive.

The Market Place appraisal describes older buildings in local stone with plain clay tile or slate, and later brick buildings with slate, and notes that slate has been lost to substitutes and concrete tiles over the years. The Park appraisal makes the same point and asks for Welsh slate or plain clay tiles on roofs there.

Source: Mansfield District Council, conservation areas, Market Place appraisal, The Park appraisal

Dormers, roof lights and the Pleasley Article 4

The council’s householder guidance says a dormer in a conservation area will always need permission, and it lists roof tiles, chimneys and pots, roof lights and solar panels among the things to ask about. The only Article 4 direction in a Mansfield conservation area is at Pleasley Park and Vale, where altering a roof slope that faces the road needs permission.

Source: Guidance for householders, Pleasley Park and Vale
